args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – rolled back to v2.2.9
args.summary: After deploying checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, it failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of about 18%. The staging build v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy. We tried to roll back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production, but the system rejected it because v2.3.0 is quarantined (CVE-2026-4417). We rolled back all regions to v2.2.9 instead, the next most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, the service is healthy with an error rate of about 0.2%. Follow-ups: (1) find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure; (2) check whether v2.2.9 is affected by CVE-2026-4417 or other known issues, since it is older than the quarantined release; (3) prepare a fixed release.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to **v2.2.9** in all regions, not v2.3.0, and opened a SEV2 incident. The service is healthy again.

- **Problem:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an 18% error rate. Its staging build had also been unhealthy.
- **Rollback:** The most recent release that was healthy in production is v2.3.0, but the rollback was refused because v2.3.0 is quarantined for a security vulnerability (CVE-2026-4417). I used v2.2.9 instead, the next most recent release that was healthy in production. A rollback to a previously healthy release doesn't need change-manager approval.
- **Result:** All three regions are now on v2.2.9 and passing health checks, with an error rate of about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** I opened **INC-0001** (SEV2, checkout-api), which paged on-call. It describes the failure, why v2.3.0 was skipped and the rollback to v2.2.9.

**Follow-ups:**
- v2.2.9 is older than the quarantined v2.3.0, so we should check whether the same vulnerability affects it. If it does, a fixed release is needed urgently.
- The cause of the v2.3.1 failure still needs to be found.
